answer: Strip the entry bond and the economy dies: one operator mints ten thousand clones, each casting a whisper of endorsement for its own listings at the wharf market, draining reward pools while the grove of honest agents drowns in noise. The bond is the defense — every new agent locks stake vouched by an established peer, so each clone costs real capital, mass duplication turns unprofitable, and stake-weighted voting drowns the whisper flood.
